stories.title: 📜 Infancy Gospel of Thomas
summaryBullets: At age five, Jesus plays by a stream, gathers water into pools, and commands them to obey (ch. 2).
He shapes twelve sparrows from clay and brings them to life when rebuked for working on the Sabbath (ch. 2).
Bystanders marvel, but others accuse him of breaking the law by creating on the Sabbath (ch. 2).
Another child scatters the pools; Jesus curses him, and the boy withers (ch. 3).
A boy runs into Jesus, and Jesus declares, 'You shall not finish your course,' and the child falls dead (ch. 4).
The people complain to Joseph, fearing Jesus’ power (ch. 5).
Joseph admonishes Jesus, who answers sharply, causing further fear among the townsfolk (ch. 5).
A teacher named Zacchaeus tries to teach Jesus letters, but Jesus explains the hidden meanings of Alpha and Beta (ch. 6).
The teacher marvels at his wisdom, saying no man can comprehend such mysteries (ch. 6).
Other teachers are confounded, unable to correct or control him (ch. 7).
Jesus reveals knowledge beyond human learning, silencing the elders (ch. 8).
Jesus heals a child struck down, raising him alive again (ch. 9).
He miraculously lengthens a beam of wood to help Joseph in carpentry (ch. 10).
He provides corn for the poor and heals many who come to him (ch. 11).
The people marvel, saying God is working through him, though some still fear his power (ch. 11).
At age twelve, Jesus travels with his parents to Jerusalem for the Passover (ch. 19).
He stays behind in the Temple, sitting among teachers and questioning them (ch. 19).
All marvel at his understanding and answers, recognizing divine wisdom in him (ch. 19).
Mary and Joseph find him and he replies, 'Do you not know I must be about my Father’s business?' (ch. 19).
crossRefs: Genesis 2:2–3 — God rests on the seventh day.
Mark 2:27 — The Sabbath made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
Luke 13:15–16 — Healing on the Sabbath challenged.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׁבָּת (šabbāt) — Greek: σάββατον (sábbaton) — Aramaic: שבּתא (šabbātā)
translationNotes.note: Day of rest in Jewish law; controversy arises from Jesus’ creative act on this day.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jesus shows miraculous power over nature, even as a child, leading to conflict about Sabbath law.
